name: Hindustan Unilever Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest FMCG company: Home Care (detergents, dishwash), Beauty & Personal Care (skin, hair, oral), and Foods & Refreshment (tea, coffee, Horlicks, Kissan). Ice cream was demerged into Kwality Wall's India (model knowledge; Q1 FY27 sales growth reported by that entity). 61.9% owned by Unilever. At a Capital Markets Day in Sept 2026 HUL set a 22-24% EBITDA-margin ambition and raised capex intent to ~3% of turnover. Q2 FY27 sales Rs 18,226 cr (+14.5% y/y) with margin pressure from rising input costs.

cost_structure.note: crude-linked chemicals (LAB, surfactants) and plastics packaging, approximate

exposures.mechanism: Crude-linked surfactants/LAB and polymer packaging ~18% of costs (approx., model knowledge). +10% Brent => derivatives +6% => costs +1.1% => at costs 77% of sales = 0.83% of sales => EBITDA -3.6% at 23% margin; pricing offsets ~50% => -1.8%; persistence 0.5, EV/MCap 1.0 => -0.9. Empirical -0.38 (t=-1.0) agrees on sign and is smaller. Livemint 2026-10-28 reports margin pressure from crude.

evidence.note: Livemint: HUL faces margin pressure as crude prices surge and input costs rise

exposures.mechanism: Palm-derived fatty acids/noodle oil ~10% of costs. +10% => costs +1.0% => 0.77% of sales => EBITDA -3.3%; 50% pass-through => -1.7; persistence 0.5 => -0.8. India cut edible-oil import duty on 24 Sep 2026, a partial offset.

evidence.note: Reuters: India cuts edible oil import duty ahead of festivals

exposures.mechanism: Tea/coffee (Brooke Bond, Bru) ~6% of costs. +15% => costs +0.9% => 0.7% of sales => EBITDA -3.0%; 60% pricing recovery => -1.2; persistence 0.5 => -0.6.

Packaging 10% of costs (partly overlaps crude; kept for paper/board and film not tied to Brent). +10% => costs +1.0% => EBITDA -3.3% => 50% passthrough => -1.7 x 0.5 persistence => -0.8; shaded to -0.6 to avoid double count with F_BRENT.

~12% of inputs imported/USD-linked. +3% => costs +0.36% => 0.28% of sales => EBITDA -1.2%; pass-through half => persistence 0.5 => -0.3; rounded to -0.5 including royalty-related USD sentiment. Royalty to Unilever is a % of INR turnover (no FX).

Rural ~36-40% of sales (model knowledge). +5pp rural growth => group volume +1.8% x 40% incremental margin / 23% margin => EBITDA +3.1% x persistence 0.5 => +1.5. Weak 2026 monsoon is the live risk; HUL volume growth recovered in Q2 per company.

evidence.note: Moneycontrol: weak monsoon pressures rural demand
Moneycontrol: HUL up after Q2 on volume growth optimism

exposures.mechanism: Urban ~60% of sales; premium beauty/personal care. +5pp urban => sales +3% x 40% incremental margin / 23% => EBITDA +5.2% x persistence 0.5 => +2.6; trimmed to +2.0 for overlap with rural.

evidence.note: Deccan Herald: consumers are back, stocks aren't

exposures.mechanism: P/E 41.6, 92% payout, debt-free: duration-like multiple. +25bp repo => ~-1.0 on valuation. No funding-cost channel.

A further broad GST cut adds to affordability after the Sept 2025 reform that lowered rates on many personal-care/food items (model knowledge). +1 => volume +1.5% => EBITDA +2.5% x persistence 0.5 => +1.0; Oct 2026 GST ITC easing also noted.

evidence.note: Outlook Money: FMCG rally as GST Council eases ITC rules

exposures.mechanism: Strategy shift toward premium beauty, wellbeing, new categories (Capital Markets Day Sept 2026). +1 => mix adds ~0.5pp gross margin => EBITDA +2% x persistence 1.0 x 0.5 execution haircut => +1.0.

evidence.note: ET/Moneycontrol: Capital Markets Day; 22-24% EBITDA margin target

exposures.mechanism: Quick-commerce favours D2C and small brands (competition) but is also a growth channel for HUL's premium range; net near zero, low confidence.
FII holding fell from 10.1% to 9.26% in two quarters; stock at ~6-year lows (Business Standard 2026-10-27). +US$5bn inflow => ~+1.0 for a large defensive.
